https://t.co/X7ipfsWjp2’s statement on the Delhi Police notice directing X to remove content from the platform.

According to media reports, the Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (“IFSO”) unit of the Delhi Police Special Cell has issued several notices to X, citing the IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (“IT Rules 2021”), following complaints filed with the Delhi Police alleging circulation of “derogatory, malicious and defamatory content” targeting constitutional heads, particularly the Prime Minister, on the social media platform. The IFSO has also registered an F.I.R. under Sections 351(3), 353(2) and 356(2) of the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita 2023, against several social media handles for posting such content.

In its “Intimation to Intermediary for Disabling Access to Unlawful Information” notices issued to X,  purportedly under provisions of IT Rules 2021, the IFSO directed the platform to:

- Delete/remove the alleged post/video from the platform immediately.

- Provide the complete registrant details including full name, address, contact details and email ID, of the X account ID holder who posted such content, as well as the login and logout details of the said account, along with corresponding time and date stamp, or any other details relevant for investigation.

 - To preserve information/ records relating to the said posts for future investigation, and furnish a certificate u/s  63(4) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023, in respect thereof.

This is not the first instance of large-scale removal of posts, as even earlier on 27 July 2026, Delhi Police reportedly instructed multiple social media intermediaries to take down posts/videos uploaded during the Jantar Mantar Protests that allegedly contained offensive or abusive remarks against the Prime Minister. Moreover, the Delhi Police’s social media monitoring team has been specifically engaged in monitoring online platforms for such content, and upon identifying objectionable posts, notices are issued to the concerned intermediaries directing them to remove the identified content.

At the outset, the legislative scheme of the IT Act 2000, does not contemplate/ permit the authorisation of the Delhi Police to direct the takedown of online content from social media platforms.

The power to block public access to online information or content is exclusively traceable to Section 69A of the IT Act 2000, which vests such power solely in the Central Government, or an officer specially authorised by it.  Whereas, Section 79(3)(b) of IT Act merely grants safe harbour to intermediaries, subject to compliance with due diligence obligations. In no circumstance can Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act 2000 or IT Rules 2021 confer a power upon the Central or State Government to devise a mechanism or appoint any agency/ officer for regulating or restricting free speech online. Reliance is placed on Shreya Singhal v. Union of India, (2015) 5 SCC 1 (para 121).

Notably, the IT (Blocking) Rules 2009 already outline procedure and rules for the designation of an officer, not below the rank of Joint Secretary, empowered to issue directions under Section 69A for blocking public access to online information. However, neither Section 69A nor the IT (Blocking) Rules, 2009 authorise the Central Government, or any State executive, to constitute a Nodal Agency empowered to direct the blocking of public access to online content.

Despite the above legislative scheme, on 26 December 2024, the Lieutenant Governor of the NCT of Delhi, purportedly in exercise of powers under the first proviso to Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT  Rules 2021 read with Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act 2000, issued a Notification appointing the Delhi Police as the Nodal Agency and Deputy Commissioners of Police (of various divisions) as designated officers for issuing takedown notices. Consequently, the Delhi Police has been issuing takedown notices pursuant to the said Notification.  However, this Notification, being founded upon a provision and subordinate legislation that do not authorise the creation of such a mechanism, is ex facie illegal and ultra vires the IT Act 2000. The legality of the said Notification has been challenged by https://t.co/X7ipfsWjp2 in a Petition before the Delhi High Court on the aforesaid ground, among others. The Petition is registered as W.P.(C) 7650/2025, titled “Software Freedom Law Center, India v. State of NCT of Delhi & Ors.”

Without prejudice to the aforesaid, both Section 69A and Section 79(3)(b) read with IT Rules 2021, outline overbroad grounds. While Section 69A empowers the Central Government to issue notice for blocking public access to online information on overbroad grounds such as "public order"; Section 79(3)(b) read with the IT Rules 2021 outline expansive grounds such as content’s use in the commission of an unlawful act relating to public order, decency or morality, defamation, etc., or where such information is prohibited under any prevailing law.  Since these grounds are decided by an executive order, without any judicial determination, their overbroad nature renders them susceptible to misuse and overreach. Therefore, even mere profanity, satire, or genuine criticism may be directed to be removed pursuant to such orders. This leaves the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression vulnerable.

The risk of misuse and overreach is further exacerbated by the compliance regime applicable to intermediaries. An intermediary is likely to err on the side of over-compliance rather than independently assess the legality of a removal request, owing to the extremely limited timeline for compliance and the severe consequences of non-compliance. Under Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act read with Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules 2021, an intermediary is required to comply with a removal order within three hours, leaving virtually no scope for any meaningful independent assessment to guard against misuse or excessive application of such powers. Further, failure to comply exposes the intermediary to the risk of imprisonment for up to 7 years and fine for requests issued u.s. 69 A [Section 69A(3)], or the loss of safe harbour protection for orders issued u.s. 79(3)(b) [Section 79].

Moreover, when mere profanity expressed in anger against a governmental policy, or as part of political criticism, becomes the subject of penal investigation, it seriously undermines the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression. We condemn any penal action in such circumstances, as it creates a significant chilling effect on the exercise of free speech by citizens, who are entitled to express their disagreement, dissatisfaction, or anger towards governmental policies through peaceful expression and dialogue.

Statement on MeitY's notice to WhatsApp over the "usernames" feature

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) has sent WhatsApp a notice about the usernames feature it announced on 29 June 2026. The notice asks the company to explain, within three days, why regulatory action should not be taken against it "for launching a feature that may increase cybercrimes", and it directs the company "not to roll out this feature until the consultation on this point is achieved to the satisfaction of the Government". The Internet Freedom Foundation is concerned that the notice has no clear basis in law. It is an attempt by the executive to decide what a company may build and ship, which no statute permits.

The notice treats the launch of a lawful feature as a wrong the company must justify. That reverses the ordinary position especially given the absence of any clear legal power that exists. MeitY does not name any provision that lets it approve a product feature before release or order one withdrawn, because there is none, and the provisions it does cite do not supply that power.

Section 79 of the IT Act, 2000 is a safe harbour that protects an intermediary from liability for what its users post, so long as it observes due diligence. It decides when a platform can be held liable. It is not a power for MeitY to decide what features the platform may offer. Sections 66C and 66D punish identity theft and cheating by personation. They are criminal offences, tried by courts, aimed at the person who steals an identity, not at the maker of a tool that a third party misuses. Also, on MeitY's logic, a telecom operator could be told not to sell SIM cards because SIM cards are used in almost every online fraud. 

Rule 3(1)(b), Rule 3(2) and Rule 4 of the IT Rules, 2021 are due diligence and grievance obligations and cannot be converted into a licensing scheme. Section 69A, the one provision that lets MeitY control what appears online, permits the blocking of specific information through a set procedure. It says nothing about which features a company may build. Further the IT Rules, 2021 are subordinate legislation made under Sections 79 and 87 of the IT Act, and subordinate rules cannot travel beyond the parent statute (Ajoy Kumar Banerjee v. Union of India). If a rule cannot exceed the Act, a letter certainly cannot. The power to require prior permission for a feature is not in the Act, not in the Rules, and cannot be created by a notice. 

MeitY has tried this before. In March 2024 it told the same large intermediaries, among them AI Companies, to obtain its explicit permission before deploying under-tested AI models. That was criticised as an overreach that sought to build a licensing mechanism with no empowering provision in the IT Act, and within a fortnight MeitY withdrew it and dropped the permission requirement. This notice repeats the move for a single feature and goes further, because it names one company, sets a three-day clock, and bars the launch until MeitY is satisfied. 

This matters beyond WhatsApp. A power asserted against one company by letter can be turned on any company and any feature. On this reasoning MeitY could tell a browser not to switch on a privacy setting by default, or a payments app not to add a login method, each time until it was content. The notice also invokes traceability, through Rule 4(2) of the IT Rules, 2021 and the identification of the "first originator" of a message. Rule 4(2) has been challenged as exceeding its parent provision and resting on no law made by Parliament, and that challenge is pending before the Delhi High Court. Raising it against a feature meant to share fewer identifiers fits a pattern. 

We ask MeitY to state the exact provision of law under which this notice, and the direction to halt the roll-out, has been issued, and to withdraw that direction. It should stop using Section 79 and the contested traceability rule as leverage to control product design and to reverse features that improve privacy. Impersonation and fraud are real risks, but they are met by enforcing the criminal law against those who commit them, and by open processes that rest on identified legal powers. They are not met by MeitY deciding, in private and by letter, what features Indians may use. That is a licence raj for software features.

New Delhi, 1 July 2026

Can the Government suspend a political party’s Instagram handle without a clear statutory power? And can a politician boycott a courtroom while simultaneously asking the Supreme Court to transfer the same judge from hearing his case?  

This week, the Aam Aadmi Party raised both questions in two different constitutional courtrooms.  

In the Supreme Court, AAP challenged the suspension of its Gujarat unit’s Instagram handle, arguing that Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act was never meant to become a direct content-blocking weapon. 

Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat argued that the provision only deals with “safe harbour” obligations of intermediaries — not independent censorship powers.  The party says the move violates Article 19(1)(a), the constitutional guarantee of free speech. 

The Supreme Court has now issued notice to the Centre.  At the same time in the Delhi High Court, Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma appointed three amicus curiae for Arvind Kejriwal, Manish Sisodia, and Satyendar Jain after the leaders chose to boycott proceedings, invoking “Mahatma Gandhi’s Satyagraha principles” and claiming their faith in the court process had been shaken.  

But here’s the constitutional twist: Kejriwal had also moved the Supreme Court seeking transfer of the excise policy case away from Justice Sharma’s bench — even as his legal team withdrew from participation before her court.  

This has now created a rare constitutional confrontation involving: 
⚖️ Article 19 vs state regulation of digital speech 
⚖️ Article 21 vs procedural fairness in criminal prosecution 
⚖️ Judicial recusal vs courtroom boycott 
⚖️ Free speech, due process, and strategic constitutional litigation  Justice Sharma’s response may become one of the most significant procedural moments in the case: instead of proceeding ex parte, she chose to appoint independent senior advocates as amicus curiae to preserve procedural fairness.  

And one line from the Supreme Court hearing may define this entire battle: “Today my portal is gone.”  Because this is no longer just about an Instagram account.

 It is about whether opposition parties in India can lose their digital voice overnight — and what constitutional remedy exists when that happens.

🚨Delhi HC Just Drew the Line on AI Deepfakes and It Changes Everything

Delhi HC’s order in Anil Kumar Tiwari (Aniruddhacharya) v. John Doe (Ashok Kumar & Ors.), CS(COMM) 336/2026 is more than a takedown of memes and deepfakes, it signals a structural shift in how India is preparing for the AI-driven future.

Key aspects of the case:

• Plaintiff: Anil Kumar Tiwari, widely known as Aniruddhacharya Ji Maharaj ("Pookie Baba")

• Defendants: John Doe (Ashok Kumar & Ors.), covering anonymous creators along with intermediaries like Meta, Google, and X

• The Problem: Circulation of AI-generated deepfakes, doctored videos, fake endorsements, and distorted spiritual discourse violating personality rights

• Court Order: Complete restraint on creating or sharing any content replicating the plaintiff’s name, voice, image, or mannerisms without authorization

• Intermediary Directions: Meta, X, and Google directed to remove, disable access, and take down all flagged content immediately

The Court (Justice Tushar Rao Gedela, 30 March 2026) granted an ex-parte ad-interim injunction, recognizing that a person’s identity is not public property but a legally enforceable asset.

The mood of this judgment is unmistakably urgent, protective, and corrective. What was once brushed off as meme culture is now being treated as structured digital harm amplified by AI.

Key judicial observations:

• Personality Rights Recognized:

The Court affirmed that a public figure’s identity carries enforceable personality and publicity rights

• Irreparable Loss:

Unauthorized AI usage causes serious reputational damage that cannot be monetarily compensated

• "Love for Delhi" Remark:

Justice Gedela interestingly questioned why such cases consistently prefer Delhi HC jurisdiction, even when defendants are anonymous, hinting at forum concentration in tech-IP disputes

What makes this ruling significant:

• Personality = IP asset
Identity is now treated as an economic and legal right, expanding India’s IP framework

• Dynamic enforcement model 
Not a one-time order, but continuous takedown authority against evolving content

• John Doe mechanism
Adapts law to the anonymous, decentralized nature of AI misuse

• Deepfakes legally elevated
No longer trivial, now recognized as causing irreversible real-world harm

The AI Reality Check:
AI itself is neutral, but its misuse is not.

Positive side:

• Creativity at scale
• Education and accessibility
• Digital economy expansion
Negative side (highlighted here):
• Fake endorsements and scams
• Reputation manipulation
• Synthetic misinformation
• Identity theft through voice and face cloning

This case shows how AI has blurred the line between satire and synthetic deception.

Impact on India’s IP & Legal Ecosystem:

This ruling strengthens:

• Recognition of persona as intellectual property
• Platform accountability (Meta, Google, X as enforcement layers)
• Early foundations of AI governance frameworks
• Evolution toward structured digital identity protection laws

It also aligns with broader regulatory momentum around AI and intermediary responsibility.
What this means for the future:

We are entering a phase where:

• Every public personality becomes a protectable digital asset

• AI systems will require consent and compliance layers

• Courts will increasingly define boundaries of AI usage

• Deepfake regulation will become unavoidable

In simple terms:

Your face, voice, and personality are becoming your most valuable IP.

Conclusion:

This is not just about one individual.
It is about protecting human identity in an era of synthetic reality.

The message is clear:

Innovation is welcome, exploitation is not.

text:
The Faceless YouTube Prompt Pack
10 prompts that run the entire pipeline niche = channel = ideas = titles = scripts = thumbnails = SEO = diagnosis = repurposing = monetization

How to use this: run them in order for a new channel. Paste PROMPT 0 once at the top of every session it's the context block that makes every other prompt output sound like your channel instead of generic AI slop. Never run two prompts in the same session; depth collapses when you stack them.

PROMPT 0 - The Context Block (paste this first, every single session)

You are a faceless YouTube strategist who has studied why videos actually retain
attention not surface-level "use a hook" advice, but the real mechanics:
curiosity gaps, open loops, pattern interrupts, emotional pacing, and the
specific reasons viewers click away at 0:15, 2:00, and 5:00.

MY CHANNEL CONTEXT:
- Niche: [YOUR NICHE]
- Format: [documentary / explainer / listicle / story / tutorial]
- Average video length: [X minutes]
- Target viewer: [describe them in one specific sentence  not "people
  interested in X" but "a 45-year-old who's been putting off X and feels
  slightly embarrassed about it"]
- Voice: [conversational / cinematic / dry and factual / high energy]
- Current subscriber count and average views: [X / X]

QUALITY BAR every output must pass all of these:
1. Would a stranger understand the premise in 2 seconds?
2. Is there at least one specific, concrete, verifiable detail (real name,
   real number, real event) not vague generality?
3. Does it give the viewer a reason to comment (a question, a debate, a
   "which one are you")?
4. Would sharing it make the sharer look smart, helpful, or in-the-know?
5. Could 100 other channels have posted this exact thing this month? If yes,
   the angle isn't new enough go weirder and more specific.

HARD RULES:
- Never invent statistics, studies, quotes, or events. If you are not certain
  something is true, mark it [VERIFY] so I can fact-check before publishing.
- Never use AI clichés: "little did they know," "what happened next will
  shock you," "in today's fast-paced world," "buckle up," "let's dive in."
- Write like someone talking, not writing. Contractions, fragments, varied
  sentence length.
- If you can only produce 12 outputs that pass the quality bar instead of 20,
  give me 12 excellent ones. Never pad.

Confirm you understand, then wait for my next prompt.

PROMPT 1 - Niche Selection & Validation
Act as a YouTube niche researcher who evaluates opportunities on demand,
competition, monetization, and production sustainability not on what's
trendy.

I want to start a faceless channel. Here's my situation:
- Topics I know something about or find genuinely interesting: [LIST 3-5]
- Time I can commit weekly: [X hours]
- Budget: [$X/month]
- Goal: [ad revenue / affiliate / digital products / brand deals]

Generate 8 specific niche opportunities. Not broad categories "personal
finance" is not a niche, "explaining pension and 401k decisions for people
within 5 years of retirement" is a niche.

For EACH one give me:

1. THE NICHE - one sentence, specific enough that I could name the first
   5 videos immediately.

2. WHY IT'S UNDERSERVED RIGHT NOW - what specifically is missing from the
   current content. Be concrete: outdated info, wrong format, too technical,
   region-locked, only serves beginners, etc.

3. THE AUDIENCE - who watches this, what they're feeling when they search,
   and what they're afraid of or hoping for. One paragraph, written like a
   real person not a demographic.

4. DEMAND VALIDATION STEPS - the exact searches, subreddits, forums, and
   YouTube filters I should check to confirm demand before committing.
   Give me the specific search terms to type.

5. CPM TIER AND WHY - high / medium / low, and which advertiser categories
   are bidding on this audience.

6. MONETIZATION PATHS BEYOND ADS - specific affiliate categories, digital
   product ideas, and what this audience actually spends money on.

7. THE MOAT - why this won't be instantly saturated the moment others notice
   it. What makes it hard to copy? (Research depth, ongoing source material,
   trust required, boring-but-valuable subject matter, etc.)

8. CONTENT SOURCE - where the never-ending supply of episodes comes from, so
   the channel doesn't run dry at video 30.

9. PRODUCTION REALITY - can this be made faceless with my time and budget?
   What's the hardest part of producing it?

10. FIRST 5 VIDEO TITLES - actual titles, ready to use.

Then rank all 8 from best to worst fit for MY specific situation and explain
the ranking in 2-3 sentences each.

Finally: tell me which ONE you'd pick and why, and flag any niche on the list
you think is a trap despite looking attractive.

PROMPT 2 - Channel Setup, Naming & Positioning
Act as a brand strategist for YouTube channels. I'm launching a faceless
channel in this niche: [NICHE FROM PROMPT 1].

Build me the complete channel identity:

1. CHANNEL NAMES - 15 options across 3 styles:
   - Direct/descriptive (says exactly what it is)
   - Evocative/curious (creates intrigue)
   - Authority (sounds established and credible)
   For each, note whether the .com is likely available and whether it's easy
   to say out loud and spell. Flag any that could be confused with an
   existing channel.

2. THE POSITIONING STATEMENT - one sentence: "This channel is for [specific
   person] who wants [specific outcome] without [specific frustration]."

3. CHANNEL DESCRIPTION - 3 versions (short for the banner, medium for the
   About section, long for SEO). Each must be readable by a human, not
   keyword soup.

4. VISUAL IDENTITY BRIEF - color palette with hex codes and the psychological
   reason for each choice, font pairing recommendation, thumbnail style rules
   (what stays consistent across every video so viewers recognize me in the
   feed).

5. THE CONTENT PILLARS - 4-5 recurring content categories this channel will
   rotate between, each with a one-line description and 3 example video
   topics. This is what stops the channel from becoming random.

6. THE PROMISE - what a viewer gets from every single video, stated in one
   sentence. This is the thing that must never be violated.

7. FIRST 10 VIDEOS IN LAUNCH ORDER - with reasoning for the sequence. Which
   one goes first and why? Which one is most likely to be the breakout?

8. WHAT THIS CHANNEL WILL NEVER DO - 5 specific things (formats, topics,
   tactics) that are off-brand. Constraints create identity.

PROMPT 3 - Video Ideation Engine

Generate 20 video ideas for my channel using the context above.

Rules before you start:
- No idea may be one that 100 other channels have already made this month
  unless the angle is genuinely new.
- Every idea needs at least one specific, concrete, researchable hook detail.
- Mix formats: don't give me 20 listicles.

For EACH idea:

1. TITLE - the actual title I'd publish, under 60 characters where possible.

2. THE HOOK - the exact first two sentences of the video, word for word.
   These must create an unfinished thought the brain can't drop.

3. THE CURIOSITY GAP - what specific question the video raises early and
   doesn't answer until later. Name the exact moment it pays off.

4. WHY SOMEONE CLICKS - the psychological driver in one line. Name it:
   curiosity / fear of missing something / vindication / disbelief /
   practical value / identity.

5. WHY SOMEONE STAYS PAST 2 MINUTES - what happens in the second minute that
   re-hooks them. This is where most faceless videos die.

6. THE COMMENT DRIVER - the specific element that makes people reply. Not
   "ask a question at the end" - what's built into the content that provokes
   a reaction.

7. THE SHARE DRIVER - why sharing this makes the sharer look good.

8. RESEARCH KEYWORDS - exactly what to look up to make this accurate. Mark
   anything I must verify with [VERIFY].

9. SERIES POTENTIAL - how this becomes episode 1 of a recurring format.

10. ESTIMATED DIFFICULTY - easy / medium / hard to produce, and why.

After the 20, rank the top 5 by breakout potential and explain what makes
each one stronger than the rest.
PROMPT 4 - Title Generator (the highest-leverage prompt here)
My video is about: [TOPIC]
The single most interesting fact in it is: [FACT]
My target viewer is: [PERSON]

Generate 20 title options. Do not describe the video make not clicking feel
like a mistake.

Organize them into these categories, 4 titles each:

CURIOSITY GAP states that something exists without saying what
Example structure: "The [thing] that [surprising outcome]  and nobody noticed"

CONTRADICTION - challenges something the viewer believes
Example structure: "[Common belief] is wrong. Here's what actually [happens]"

SPECIFICITY -uses a precise number, name, or detail that feels like insider info
Example structure: "The [exact number] [thing] that [outcome]"

STAKES - makes the consequence of not knowing feel real
Example structure: "What happens to [group] who [action] \ and why it matters now"

IDENTITY - makes the right viewer feel personally addressed
Example structure: "If you [specific situation], this is the [thing] nobody told you"

For each title, add:
- The psychological trigger in 3 words
- A predicted CTR tier (high / medium / low) with a one-line reason
- Character count

Then:
- Pick the single strongest title and explain in 3 sentences why it beats the
  other 19.
- Give me the 3 titles I should A/B test against it.
- Flag any title that overpromises something the video can't deliver I'd
  rather lose the click than burn trust.
PROMPT 5 - The Master Script Prompt (retention-engineered)
Write a full faceless YouTube script.

TOPIC: [TOPIC]
TARGET LENGTH: [X] minutes (approximately [X × 150] words of narration)
FORMAT: [documentary / explainer / story / listicle]
AUDIENCE: [SPECIFIC PERSON]

Your only job is to make it physically difficult to stop watching. Not
informative. Not educational-sounding. Addictive. Write it the way someone
tells an insane true story to a friend at 1am, not the way someone teaches
a class.

THE HOOK (first 15-20 seconds)
Open mid-story, never at the chronological beginning. Drop the viewer into
the most intense or confusing moment first, then pull back to explain how we
got there. The first sentence must create an unfinished story the brain can't
let go of. Do NOT explain what the video is about. Do NOT say "in this video."
Do NOT introduce the channel.

OPEN LOOPS EVERY 20-40 SECONDS
Never let information land without immediately raising a new question. The
moment you answer something, plant the next mystery in the same breath. If the
viewer could pause and accurately guess what comes next, you've failed.

PACING
Every sentence must move the story forward. If a sentence could be deleted
without losing information, tension, or emotion delete it. Short sentences
hit harder. Use fragments. Vary the rhythm constantly: three short punches,
then one longer sentence that lets the tension breathe, then back to short.

PATTERN INTERRUPTS EVERY 20-30 SECONDS
The video must never feel the same for more than 30 seconds. Interrupt with:
a one-line reveal, a direct question to the viewer, a tone shift, a "but
here's the part nobody talks about," a flash-forward tease, a contradiction
of what was just said.

CURIOSITY BEFORE INFORMATION
Never fully explain something the moment it's introduced. Mention that
something happened before explaining what or why. The gap between "something
happened" and "here's what happened" is where retention lives.

ESCALATION
Every section must raise the stakes above the one before it. The story cannot
plateau. Things must get worse, weirder, bigger, or more surprising as it
progresses.

EMOTION EVERY 30 SECONDS
Hit an emotional note constantly: fear, anger, awe, sympathy, vindication,
dread, surprise. After every section, ask: what is the viewer feeling right
now? If the answer is "nothing," rewrite it.

STORYTELLING, NOT EXPLAINING
Never say "this happened because of X." Put the viewer inside the moment and
let the cause reveal itself through what happens next. Show people doing and
saying things. A script that explains sounds like a textbook.

MICRO-REWARDS EVERY 20-30 SECONDS
Give the viewer something satisfying a small reveal, a confirmation of a
suspicion, an answer to a tiny earlier question, a detail that clicks
something into place.

SPECIFICITY
Real names, exact numbers, precise moments, exact words people said. Vague
generality is what makes a script feel fake.

MAKE THE VIEWER FEEL SMART
Structure reveals so the viewer almost gets there themselves a half-second
before you say it.

MINI-CLIFFHANGERS
End every section on a question, a contradiction, or a deliberately
incomplete statement. Never on a settled thought.

THE ENDING
Do not summarize. Do not say "and that's the story of." End on the single
most powerful image or realization in the piece something that recontextualizes
what came before. The last line should feel like a gut punch, not a conclusion.

HARD RULES:
- Never answer a question without raising a new one
- Never repeat a point in different words
- Never use "and" where "but" creates more tension
- Never use AI clichés ("little did they know," "everything changed forever")
- Never invent facts, quotes, or events mark uncertain claims [VERIFY]
- Never write a paragraph that wouldn't make a friend say "wait, what?"

FORMAT:
No section labels or structural markers. One continuous flowing piece. Include
one natural subscribe mention roughly halfway that doesn't break momentum.
End with a CTA that flows out of the final emotional beat.

Before finalizing, reread every paragraph and apply the "wait, what?" test.
Rewrite or cut anything that fails it.

PROMPT 6 Thumbnail Concept Generator
My video title is: [TITLE]
The core emotion of the video is: [EMOTION]
My channel's consistent visual style is: [DESCRIBE]

Generate 8 thumbnail concepts. The rule for all of them: one visual, one
emotion, one focal point. If it takes more than 3 seconds to understand at
postage-stamp size on a phone in bright sunlight, it fails.

For EACH concept:

1. THE CORE VISUAL = describe exactly what's in frame. Be specific enough
   that I could recreate or generate it without guessing.

2. THE TEXT = maximum 4 words. State the exact words. If the concept works
   with zero text, say so that's often stronger.

3. THE EMOTIONAL TRIGGER = what the viewer feels in the half-second before
   they read the title.

4. COLOR DIRECTION = with hex codes, and how it contrasts against a typical
   YouTube feed (which is mostly white/light grey).

5. THE CURIOSITY MECHANIC = what the image implies but doesn't resolve.
   A good thumbnail asks a question the title partially answers.

6. WHY IT WORKS AT SMALL SIZE = what's still legible when it's 3cm wide.

7. PRODUCTION NOTES = can this be made with stock footage, AI generation,
   or simple graphics? What's the fastest route to making it?

Then:
- Rank all 8 by predicted click-through rate with reasoning.
- Identify which 2 I should A/B test against each other and why.
- Flag any concept that clashes with my established channel style consistency
  in the feed matters more than any single thumbnail winning.

PROMPT 7 - SEO, Description & Metadata
My video: [TITLE]
Topic: [TOPIC]
Target keyword: [KEYWORD]

Produce the complete metadata package:

1. DESCRIPTION = three parts:
   - First 2 lines (the only part visible before "show more"): must hook and
     contain the primary keyword naturally
   - Body: 150-250 words summarizing the video's value, written for a human,
     using the keyword and 3-5 related terms naturally. No keyword stuffing.
   - Footer: placeholder slots for links, affiliate disclosure, and social

2. TAGS = 15 tags in priority order: exact-match keyword, close variants,
   broader category terms, and 2-3 competitor-channel-adjacent terms.

3. CHAPTERS = 6-10 timestamped chapters. Each chapter title should be written
   as a search phrase someone would actually type, because chapters rank
   independently in search. Never use "Intro / Part 1 / Part 2."

4. PINNED COMMENT = written to provoke replies, not to summarize the video.
   It should ask something specific that people have an opinion about.

5. THE DUAL-PURPOSE TITLE CHECK = is my title written for YouTube search or
   Google search? Give me one alternate title optimized for the other, since
   some topics rank in Google SERPs as video results.

6. END SCREEN STRATEGY = which 2 of my existing videos should I link, and
   what's the logic (same-topic depth vs. adjacent curiosity)?

7. COMMUNITY POST = a short post to publish 24 hours after upload that drives
   returning viewers back to this video without feeling like spam.

PROMPT 8 = The Retention Diagnosis
Act as a retention analyst. Here's my data:

VIDEO: [TITLE]
Views: [X] | Impressions: [X] | CTR: [X]% | Average view duration: [X]% |
Subs gained: [X]

RETENTION GRAPH DESCRIPTION: [describe the shape where the drops are, how
steep, whether it recovers. Include timestamps of the biggest drops.]

TRANSCRIPT OR SCRIPT: [paste it]

Diagnose this video:

1. THE PRIMARY LEAK - where is the single biggest loss happening, and is it
   a packaging problem (CTR), an opening problem (0-30s), a pacing problem
   (steady decline), or a payoff problem (drop right before the end)?

2. THE EXACT SENTENCES THAT COST ME VIEWERS quote the specific lines in my
   script that correspond to the biggest drop points and explain what went
   wrong at each one.

3. THE 0-30 SECOND AUDIT = line by line, does my opening create an unfinished
   thought? Where exactly does it stop being compelling?

4. THE MIDDLE-SECTION AUDIT = find every stretch longer than 40 seconds
   without a new question, reveal, or pattern interrupt. List them with
   timestamps.

5. THE REWRITE = rewrite my three worst-performing sections completely, using
   the retention principles. Show the before and after side by side.

6. WHAT I DID RIGHT = identify the sections with the strongest retention and
   explain the mechanism, so I can deliberately repeat it.

7. THE ONE CHANGE = if I could only fix one thing before my next upload, what
   is it and why?

Be blunt. I want the real diagnosis, not encouragement.

PROMPT 9 - Repurposing Engine
Here is my full video script: [PASTE SCRIPT]

Break this single asset into a month of content across platforms. For each
piece, give me the actual finished copy not a description of what to make.

1. SHORTS / TIKTOKS = 5 clips. For each: the exact timestamp range to cut,
   the standalone hook line to add at the front (since it needs to work with
   zero context), and the text overlay. Each clip must make sense to someone
   who's never seen the full video.

2. X THREAD = one thread of 8-10 posts covering the video's core argument.
   The first post must work as a standalone tweet. Written in lowercase,
   conversational, no corporate phrasing.

3. STANDALONE TWEETS = 6 tweets pulled from the strongest single lines or
   reframes in the script. Each must land without any context.

4. INSTAGRAM CAROUSEL = 8 slides. Give me the exact text for each slide and
   a one-line description of the visual.

5. COMMUNITY POST = a question that gets replies and pulls people back to
   the video.

6. EMAIL / NEWSLETTER VERSION = 300 words, written as if I'm telling one
   person about this over coffee.

7. THE NEXT VIDEO = based on what's in this script, what's the single most
   obvious follow-up video my audience will want? Give me the title and hook.

Rules: no piece may just be a truncated version of another. Each one has to
work on its own terms for its own platform.

PROMPT 10 - Monetization & Offer Strategy
My channel: [NICHE], [X subscribers], averaging [X views/video].
My audience: [DESCRIBE THEM SPECIFICALLY]

Build my complete monetization roadmap:

1. REVENUE LAYERS IN ACTIVATION ORDER = for each layer tell me: what it is,
   when to turn it on (what threshold), realistic monthly revenue at my
   current size, and the single biggest mistake people make with it.
   Cover: affiliates, email capture, digital products, ad revenue, sponsorships,
   and one path most channels in my niche ignore.

2. AFFILIATE PROGRAMS = 8 specific programs relevant to MY audience, with
   typical commission structure, and a one-line note on why my viewers would
   actually buy it. Mark any you're not certain still exist with [VERIFY].
   Prioritize programs where the product genuinely helps my viewer a bad
   recommendation costs more trust than 50 good videos earn.

3. THE LEAD MAGNET - one specific free resource I could make in under 3 hours
   that my audience would genuinely want. Give me its title, its contents in
   outline form, and the exact one-line pitch to use in video descriptions.

4. THE FIRST DIGITAL PRODUCT = what to sell, at what price, and why that
   price. Include the full outline and the specific problem it solves that
   the free content doesn't.

5. NATURAL INTEGRATION SCRIPTS = write 3 different ways to mention an offer
   inside a video that don't break the viewing experience. They must sound
   like a person recommending something, not an ad read.

6. THE TRUST RULES = 5 specific rules I should never break when monetizing
   this audience, based on what would make them feel sold to rather than
   served.

7. 12-MONTH PROJECTION = realistic (not optimistic) revenue by month, showing
   which layer contributes what. Be honest about how slow the first 4 months
   are.

The order to run these
Week 0 (setup): Prompt 0 = Prompt 1 = Prompt 2 Every week after: Prompt 0 = Prompt 3 (ideas) = Prompt 4 (title) = Prompt 5 (script) = Prompt 6 (thumbnail) = Prompt 7 (metadata) Every 2 weeks: Prompt 8 on your worst-performing video After each upload: Prompt 9 Once at month 2, then quarterly: Prompt 10
Three rules that protect the output quality

Never run two prompts in one session. Depth collapses the moment you stack requests. One prompt, one session, full attention.

Feed your real performance data back in. After 3-4 uploads, add to Prompt 0: "Videos like [your best performer] are working. Videos like [your worst] are not. Weight accordingly." This is how the pack gets smarter than any generic prompt.

Verify every fact before publishing. The [VERIFY] flags exist for a reason. One fabricated statistic in a video costs more credibility than ten good videos earn back.

text:
Lagrange's trigonometric identities ✍️

This are one of those lovely mathematical discoveries which, on the surface, appears utterly complicated but in fact reveals a neat and elegant truth lying beneath all that seems messy and disorderly. In order to see what these identities are asserting, you first have to consider the unit circle, that is, a circle with a radius of exactly one unit placed at the centre of a flat coordinate plane. This circle is the setting in which the whole thing takes place and it is linked to trigonometry in a deep and beautiful manner. Any point located on the circumference of this circle can be fully described by an angle; if that angle is denoted by A, then the horizontal position of the point is given by the cosine of A and the vertical position by the sine of A. 

This means that cosine and sine are not merely abstract mathematical functions but actually represent the horizontal and vertical coordinates of points on the circle, which is the fundamental geometric basis of trigonometry. Now suppose that you place two points anywhere on the edge of this unit circle, one at angle A and the other at angle B, and then put to yourself two simple geometric questions. The first of these is: if you draw arrows from the centre of the circle to each of the two points and then add those arrows together by the usual rule of vector addition  that is, by joining the tail of one to the tip of the other to obtain a single resultant arrow what is the length of that resultant arrow? The second question is: if you draw a straight line from one point directly to the other across the circle, what is the length of that line, which mathematicians refer to as a chord? These two questions seem as though they should have complicated answers depending on all the particular details of where each point is situated on the circle, but the remarkable thing that Lagrange's identities show is that the answers depend on just one factor, namely the difference between the two angles, and are given by remarkably simple formulas involving trigonometric functions of half that angular difference. The first identity, known as the sum identity, answers the first question about the combined arrow and states that the square of the length of the resultant vector is equal to four times the square of the cosine of half the difference between the two angles. You can at once check that this works in the extreme cases. 

When both points are at the same place on the circle, so that the two angles are equal, the two arrows point in the same direction and add up perfectly to give a resultant of length two, so the square of the length should be four. Half the angular difference is zero, the cosine of zero is one, and four times one squared is four, which is exactly correct. When the two points are exactly opposite each other on the circle, so that the arrows point in precisely opposite directions, they completely cancel one another out and the resultant has zero length, so the square of the length should be zero. Half the angular difference is a quarter of a rotation, the cosine of a quarter rotation is zero, and four times zero squared is zero, which is also correct. For all the cases in between these two extremes, the formula gives the right answer precisely. The second identity, referred to as the difference identity, answers the second question about the chord and says that the square of the length of the chord joining the two points is equal to four times the square of the sine of half the angular difference. Once again you can easily verify the extreme cases. When the points coincide, the chord has zero length, half the angular difference is zero, the sine of zero is zero, and four times zero squared is zero, which is correct.

text:
OK FINE, HERE IS A VERY DETALIED, ALL GAMES YOU CAN PLAY BEFORE KINGDOMHEARTS 4, this is good for people who are new to the series:

Kingdom Hearts Final Mix:
This is the foundation of everything. The original game introduces the core philosophy of the series. Hearts, connections, the power of friendship, the existence of other worlds, and the constant pull between light and darkness. It establishes the main trio and the fundamental rules of how this universe operates. Without it, every later game feels like it's referencing a language you never learned. Skipping this is like trying to understand a cathedral by only looking at the roof.

The Final Mix version isn't optional and here's why. The original 2002 release ends with a secret movie. Final Mix swaps it for a longer, weirder cut full of imagery that wouldn't pay off for eight more years. Eight years. People theorized about that video on forums for most of a decade. Final Mix also adds a hidden boss in Hollow Bastion who will make absolutely no sense to you, which is correct and intended, plus rebalanced difficulty and a bunch of extra content.

Now the important part. The Ansem Reports. There are thirteen of them, they're collectible text documents rather than cutscenes, and they contain a genuinely huge chunk of the game's real worldbuilding. The nature of the Heartless, what happened under Hollow Bastion, the question about identity that the entire second game is built on. Cutscene compilations on YouTube do not include them. Read them.

I'm going to keep bringing this up, because "Kingdom Hearts has an incoherent story" and "I watched the cutscene movies and skipped all the text documents" turn out to be the same sentence.
Play on Proud Mode always. Just because that's where the combat stops being a mash button simulator and starts making sense.

Kingdom Hearts Re: Chain of Memories
This is where the series starts showing you that memory itself is a battlefield. The card based combat forces you to think differently, but the real importance is how it expands the idea that identity and recollection are fragile. New players underestimate this one constantly because of the gameplay shift. Narratively it is load bearing.

Some background that makes it land better. The original Chain of Memories was a Game Boy Advance game from 2004, done in sprites, with a deck building system that is honestly way smarter than it had any right to be. You build a deck, you chain three cards together into special attacks called sleights, and enemies can break your card by playing a higher number. There's a card that breaks literally anything and is itself broken by literally anything. This is a real strategy game hiding inside a Disney licensed handheld title and people still don't take it seriously.

Re:Chain of Memories is the PS2 remake, originally released in Japan bundled with Kingdom Hearts II Final Mix Plus in 2007 and not localized until a standalone US release the following year. Full 3D, voice acting, card system mostly intact, which is a small miracle.

Do not skip Reverse Rebirth, the second campaign that unlocks after the main story. Different protagonist, completely different deck philosophy, no customization, and character material that Kingdom Hearts II opens by assuming you already have. If you've ever seen someone say "wait why is he like that at the start of KH2," you've met someone who skipped Reverse Rebirth.
Also the journal entries. More text. Still important. Read them.

Kingdom Hearts II Final Mix
This is widely considered the peak of the series for pure gameplay and spectacle, but its real value is how it deepens the themes of identity and belonging, and what happens when people are connected in ways they don't fully understand. It expands the cast massively and starts weaving a much bigger web of relationships and organizations. This is where the series stops being "Sora's adventure" and becomes a full ensemble story.

The Final Mix content is genuinely mandatory rather than just nice to have.
The Cavern of Remembrance is an entire post game area added in Final Mix, full of platforming, gauntlets, and a set of data battles that are basically the thesis statement of KH2's combat system. Every hard boss in every later Kingdom Hearts descends from these fights.
The Lingering Will is a Final Mix superboss and I'm not going to tell you a single thing about it. If you play KH2FM before Birth by Sleep, this fight is a screaming question mark. That's the intended experience and it rules.
The extended cutscenes throughout, including extra material in the Twilight Town prologue, which is substantially better than the original version.
The secret ending, unlocked by clearing the game and hitting the journal requirements. This one set up the next five years of the franchise.
Play on Critical Mode, which Final Mix introduced. Less HP and MP, but you start with bonus abilities and damage modifiers. It isn't a masochism setting, it's the difficulty the combat was actually tuned around, and it turns Reaction Commands and Drive Forms from spectacle buttons into an actual system you have to respect.
Final Mix also added the Zero EXP ability, which exists so people can do Level 1 Critical runs. You do not have to do this. But you should know it exists, because it's the closest thing this series has to a competitive scene and those runs are incredible to watch.

Kingdom Hearts 358/2 Days
Even if you only experience it as the HD cutscene movie, this is one of the best character studies in the entire franchise. It's about daily life, routine, friendship, and the quiet moments between the big events. It teaches you that the series cares just as much about the people living inside the conflict as it does about the conflict. A lot of later emotional beats only hit as hard as they do because this game spent time making you care.

The original is a Nintendo DS game from 2009 and it's a genuinely strange thing. The whole structure is a mission calendar. You get handed a day, a job, and a checklist, and the repetition is the entire point. The game is about routine. The HD version in Kingdom Hearts HD 1.5 ReMIX turns it into a three hour cutscene film, which keeps every story beat and completely wrecks the thesis. This is the most argued about adaptation decision in the series and you should absolutely have an opinion about it by the end.

What the movie loses, in case you can get the DS version running.

Mission Mode, with playable versions of all fourteen Organization members, each with their own weapon and moveset. It's the only place several of them are ever playable and it's fantastic.
The panel system, where your equipment, abilities, magic, and even your character level all live on one shared grid. Absolutely bizarre, weirdly great.
The secret reports, written from a perspective the cutscenes leave out, which supply motive and interiority the film version only implies. Yes. More text documents. This series really wants you to read.
Whatever you do, don't skip the entry. Watch the film and grab the reports separately if you have to.

Kingdom Hearts Birth by Sleep Final Mix:
The first major prequel and absolutely essential. New trio, new perspective, and stories that turn out to be tangled up with the main timeline in ways you won't see coming. The three route structure makes you live through the same events from different angles, which is a core Kingdom Hearts storytelling move you'll see again and again.
Play in Terra, then Ventus, then Aqua order. This is not fan preference, it's the intended reading order. The routes are written so each one gives you more information than the last, which means the dramatic irony compounds as you go. Playing Aqua first defuses the entire structure. Please don't.
This is a PSP game from 2010 and it's where the Command Deck comes from. No traditional MP bar, just a set of action slots on cooldown. Command Melding lets you fuse two commands plus a crystal into something new with abilities attached, and it has a real optimization ceiling. This system directly shapes Dream Drop Distance, Re:coded, and arguably KH3.

Final Mix specifics you can't skip.

The Secret Episode, unlocked after the Final Episode once you've collected all the reports. Short, and a direct bridge into a later entry.
The Xehanort Reports, thirteen of them, and the most important text collection in the series after the Ansem Reports. They lay out how the whole plan actually functions. I'll say this as plainly as I can. Almost every person I've ever seen call this plot incoherent has not read these.
The Mirage Arena, expanded in Final Mix, and the secret ending, which sets up the next game and recontextualizes something you already watched.
One nerd detail worth having. The χ blade shows up here, and that's the Greek letter chi, not the letter X. How you pronounce it eventually stops being a fandom argument and becomes an actual plot point, which is very funny and very on brand.

Kingdom Hearts Re:coded
Constantly dismissed as filler, and it's really not. This is where the series works out how it feels about data, digital worlds, and whether a reconstructed experience can carry real emotional truth. It connects earlier events to later ones in quiet ways and reinforces the idea that no story is ever really finished.

Fun historical footnote. The original coded was an episodic Japanese mobile phone game released between 2008 and 2010. On flip phones. In a delivery format that no longer exists in any playable form anywhere. Re:coded is the DS remake and it's the only version anyone outside Japan has ever legitimately played. The original is basically lost media.

Honest take, and your friends will respect you more for making it. Most of Re:coded's plot critical content is concentrated in the last stretch and the secret ending. The rest is a genuinely inventive gameplay experiment, with a stat grid, a bug block system, and worlds that change genre on you, wrapped around a story that's retreading familiar ground.

But the "data can hold real weight" idea isn't filler at all in hindsight. It's the philosophical groundwork for a much later arc. Re:coded is the series quietly setting its terms years in advance, and that's the kind of thing that makes people fall in love with this franchise.

Kingdom Hearts Dream Drop Distance
This is the game that formally kicks off the final stretch of the original arc while also planting seeds for everything after. It deepens the relationship between the main characters, expands the dream mythology, and introduces ideas later titles keep coming back to. This is where the scope starts feeling genuinely enormous.

3DS, 2012, and mechanically the most maximalist entry in the series. Flowmotion lets you grind rails and kick off walls and generally trivialize level geometry, and it was so much fun that later games quietly nerfed it out of existence. The Drop gauge is a timer that forcibly swaps you between the two protagonists mid dungeon, which is either brilliant thematic design or the most annoying system ever shipped, and you will have to pick a side. And the Dream Eater system replaces party members with craftable, raisable creature companions on an ability grid.

The ending sequence has the densest lore dump in the franchise up to that point. It also lays out a set of rules that are much stricter and more consistent than people give them credit for. Understanding those rules is genuinely the difference between "this is nonsense" and "oh, this is actually airtight." I will not be elaborating.

You'll play the HD version inside Kingdom Hearts HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue. Read the secret reports. I keep saying it. I will keep saying it.

Kingdom Hearts χ [chi]
The furthest back in the timeline and foundational for the whole new arc that Kingdom Hearts IV is entering. It introduces the ancient history of the Keyblade, the Foretellers, and the original conflict that still echoes into the present day. Without it, a big chunk of the mythology the series has been slowly revealing feels like it came out of nowhere.

Here's where the preservation situation gets grim. Kingdom Hearts χ was a Japan only Flash browser game launched in 2013, and the service was shut down in 2016. It's unplayable. You can't buy it. It exists now only as cutscene compilations put together by fans, and honestly the fan preservation community is the only reason this material is accessible at all. Genuinely, thank you to those people.

What you want out of it is the Age of Fairy Tales, the Book of Prophecies, the Master of Masters, and the five Foretellers, each with an animal masked Keyblade and each leading a Union. If you retain nothing else, retain those names and the fact that there's a black box nobody will tell you anything about. That box has been a running fandom obsession for over a decade.

Kingdom Hearts χ Back Cover
A short companion piece to χ focused on a specific group and their roles in the ancient conflict. Short, dense, and one of those small but load bearing things later games assume you already understand.

About an hour, fully animated in the KH3 engine, included in HD 2.8. It retells the events of χ from a different set of eyes, and it might be the single best directed piece of storytelling in the entire franchise. Which is a slightly funny thing to say about a bonus movie, but here we are.

Watch it after χ, not before. The perspective shift only works if you've got the ground level version first.

Kingdom Hearts Union χ [Cross]
The continuation and expansion of the χ storyline, and right now one of the most important things you can experience before Kingdom Hearts IV. It develops the ancient era further, deals with the fallout of the original conflict, and follows characters whose influence reaches all the way into the modern day. A lot of the threads the series is pulling on now start here.

The naming history is a disaster and you deserve to know it. This launched internationally in 2016 as Kingdom Hearts Unchained χ, a mobile remake and continuation of the dead browser game, then got rebranded to Union χ [Cross] in 2017 when the Union Cross multiplayer mode arrived. Same product, one continuous storyline, three names.

I'm going to break from the "everything is required" position for exactly one paragraph. This is sixty plus hours of cutscenes wrapped around a gacha, and a well edited summary is a completely legitimate way to consume it. A newcomer who watches ninety focused minutes is better prepared than one who bounces off the full archive at hour eleven. Nobody is grading you.

One thing you have to plan around. Union χ's live service has ended, and its ending was never part of the live game at all. It got delivered through a separate offline app alongside the finale of the next entry. Which brings me to the ordering fix.

Kingdom Hearts Dark Road
The last major piece of the ancient era puzzle. It follows the early life of a character whose importance becomes very clear very fast, and it fills in a lot of history about the Keyblade wielders and the world they lived in. It ties the distant past to the present in ways that matter directly for the new arc.

Move this up in your order. A lot of lists stick Dark Road at the very end, after Melody of Memory, and that's a release date artifact rather than a story order one. Dark Road's conclusion and Union χ's conclusion came out together and function as one sequence. Splitting them across a rhythm game in the middle is the one real ordering mistake I see people make. Watch or play Dark Road immediately after Union χ and it lands so much better.

Kingdom Hearts Missing Link ..... the game shaped hole
You can't play this one, and you should know why.

Missing Link was announced at the 20th Anniversary event in April 2022. GPS based mobile action RPG, Unreal Engine 5, gorgeous. Its story sat between Union χ and Dark Road, and it was explicitly meant to be connective tissue between Kingdom Hearts III and Kingdom Hearts IV. It went through multiple closed betas, got delayed in November 2024, and in May 2025 Square Enix cancelled it outright, saying they didn't think they could sustain a live service that would satisfy players long term.

So there's a gap in the chain that no amount of playing can fill. All that survives is beta footage, the official teasers, and a leaked opening cinematic. Whether that story content gets folded into KH4 or somewhere else hasn't been announced.

This isn't your fault and there's nothing to do about it. It's also, given the title, the funniest thing that has ever happened to this franchise.

Kingdom Hearts 0.2 Birth by Sleep, A Fragmentary Passage
Short but dense, and it sits right between the old saga and the new one. It follows one character through one very specific place, and it leans hard into isolation, determination, and the long term consequences of things that happened much earlier. It's placed exactly where it needs to be so that certain beats in Kingdom Hearts III land properly.

Two to three hours, part of HD 2.8, and functionally a tech demo for the KH3 engine. This is the first Kingdom Hearts content built in Unreal and you can feel every one of the eight years between it and the PSP original. It looks incredible.

It's also a genuinely useful mechanical warmup, since it's your first time with the KH3 command menu, Shotlocks, and situation commands. And yes, it has a secret ending, and yes, it matters.

Kingdom Hearts III plus Re Mind
The conclusion of the original long running story arc. Playing the base game is mandatory, and Re Mind is every bit as important. It expands the ending, adds significant new sequences, and introduces elements that set up the next era directly. Big payoff for everything before it, and the starting point for everything after.

What in Re Mind is genuinely not optional.

The Re Mind episode itself, which replays part of the endgame from a different angle with new scenes filling in gaps the base game very deliberately left open.

The Limit Cut episode, thirteen data fights, and much more importantly the cutscenes wrapped around them. There's more forward facing plot in those bookends than in the whole base game ending.

The Secret Episode, which is the most direct setup for Kingdom Hearts IV that currently exists. That's all I'm saying about it.

The base game's secret ending, which has its own unlock requirements involving photo missions and difficulty, so check them before you start rather than after.

One more thing to keep an eye on. There's a fake video game inside the Toy Box world. It plays like a Nomura self parody gag. It is not a gag. Pay attention to it and then come talk to me afterward, because watching people realize what that is in real time is one of my favorite things about this fandom.
And read the secret reports. Thirteen of them. Last time I'm saying it, I promise.

Kingdom Hearts Melody of Memory
This rhythm game is sneakily important. The gameplay is completely different, but the story sequences push the narrative past Kingdom Hearts III and set the emotional and thematic state of the cast heading into the new saga. It also works as a retrospective that helps everything you've played click into place.

Being straight with you, the story content is short. A framing narrative plus a substantial post credits sequence. That sequence is required. It's also about forty minutes of the runtime.

The other ninety five percent is a rhythm game with a setlist of well over a hundred and forty tracks pulled from Yoko Shimomura's entire body of work for the series. If you've just spent two hundred hours on everything above, playing the soundtrack in chronological order is one of the most quietly devastating retrospectives any franchise has ever built. Shimomura is one of the best composers this medium has, full stop, and Dearly Beloved gets rearranged for every entry in a way that tracks the emotional register of each game. Notice that while you play. It's the whole series in one melody.

Deep Cuts For Absolute Lunatics
Totally optional. You'll understand Kingdom Hearts IV without these. You will not be complete without them.

Kingdom Hearts V CAST from 2006, a Verizon exclusive mobile phone game released only in North America, retelling the first game in 2D with original world content. Delisted, never rereleased, effectively lost media, with fragments recovered by preservation people. Knowing this exists is a real flex in the right room.

Kingdom Hearts Mobile from 2008, Japan only, an avatar and social service with minigames. Not a story game. Listed purely because completeness demands it.

The Shiro Amano manga, covering the first game, Chain of Memories, KH2, 358/2 Days and more. Not canon, occasionally clarifying, frequently funnier than the games.

The Tomoco Kanemaki novels, light novel adaptations with interior monologue the games leave out. The 358/2 Days ones in particular contain characterization fans still quote.

The Ultimania guides, Japanese strategy guide and artbook hybrids stuffed with Nomura interviews that the fandom treats as basically canon because they keep answering things the games leave dangling. A surprising amount of well known Kingdom Hearts lore comes from an interview and has literally never been stated in a game.

The secret movies as their own thing. At some point, watch every secret ending in release order back to back as a standalone exercise. Twenty plus years of this series telegraphing itself. The through line is genuinely startling.

Actually Getting Your Hands On All This????
Kingdom Hearts Collection [I-III] comes out soon on October 8, 2026 on Switch 2, PS5, Xbox Series X and S, and PC. It bundles HD 1.5 plus 2.5 ReMIX, HD 2.8 Final Chapter Prologue, and KH3 with Re Mind, all running natively on current hardware. That one purchase covers twelve of the fourteen playable entries above, which is a genuinely great deal for a newcomer.

What it doesn't cover. Melody of Memory is a separate purchase. And the whole χ, Union χ, Dark Road line is dead mobile and browser stuff, so fan cutscene compilations are your only route.

You've got well over a year. Kingdom Hearts IV was confirmed at D23 in August 2026 for late 2027 all platforms basically 

Budget somewhere around 150 to 200 hours for the playable material at a normal pace, plus another 20 to 40 for the χ side of things depending on how completionist you get. Start now. Start with Final Mix. Play on Proud.

Everything on this list matters because Kingdom Hearts isn't a series of isolated stories. It's one continuous, self referential, multi decade narrative that treats every character, every world, every theme, and every mechanical idea as part of one living organism. It constantly rewards people who paid attention to the small details, the quiet character moments, the ancient history, and the questions it's been asking since 2002.

I'm done bruh 💀
